LESSON: WRITING 3.3.1 SEQUENCING IDEAS

Grade: Grade 4
Subject: INDIGENOUS LANGUAGES
Strand: Strand 3
Topic 3.3: Writing 3.3.1 Sequencing Ideas
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 2

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Writing 3.3.1 Sequencing Ideas, part of Strand 3 in Grade 4 INDIGENOUS LANGUAGES.

Key inquiry question: Why should we sequence ideas in a story?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

A. identify main ideas in a simple paragraph for comprehension,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Writing 3.3.1 Sequencing Ideas in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

B. compose a paragraph on the theme for self- expression,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Writing 3.3.1 Sequencing Ideas in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

C. value the need to sequence ideas well in writing based on the theme.

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Writing 3.3.1 Sequencing Ideas in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

A. identify main ideas in a simple paragraph for comprehension,

   Writing 3.3.1 Sequencing Ideas helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

B. compose a paragraph on the theme for self- expression,

   Writing 3.3.1 Sequencing Ideas helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

C. value the need to sequence ideas well in writing based on the theme.

   Writing 3.3.1 Sequencing Ideas helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

D. Suggested learning experiences (from KICD)

1. work in partnership with peers to identify verbs in sentences from newspaper cuttings,

2. collaborate with peers to pick out the main ideas in a passage and peer review,

3. engage in a digital language game to drag and drop word segments to create simple sentences,

4. reorganise jumbled up sentences to make a well sequenced paragraph,

5. write a short paragraph on the theme with well sequenced ideas,

6. collaborate with peers to publish their final paragraph in the class or school magazine.

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

1. work in partnership with peers to identify verbs in sentences from newspaper cuttings,
2. collaborate with peers to pick out the main ideas in a passage and peer review,
3. engage in a digital language game to drag and drop word segments to create simple sentences,
4. reorganise jumbled up sentences to make a well sequenced paragraph,
5. write a short paragraph on the theme with well sequenced ideas,
6. collaborate with peers to publish their final paragraph in the class or school magazine.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Writing 3.3.1 Sequencing Ideas together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
• Digital Literacy: This is enhanced as the learner interacts with technology in a digital language game to drag and drop word

segments to create a simple sentence.

• Creativity and Imagination: This is promoted as the learner exchanges new ideas when composing paragraphs on the theme

to present well-sequenced ideas.

18

Values:
• Respect: This is enhanced as the learner takes into account other learner’s opinions during the peer review.

• Responsibility: This is enhanced as the learner diligently uses the digital devices to play digital language games as guided.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs):

ICT: This is promoted as the learner is able to learn how to engage with technology when playing a digital game to create

simple sentences.

Link to other Learning Areas:

The learner can relate concepts on paragraph writing to their learning of similar concepts in English and Kiswahili.

19

Main points to remember:

1. identify main ideas in a simple paragraph for comprehension,
2. compose a paragraph on the theme for self- expression,
3. value the need to sequence ideas well in writing based on the theme.

Remember the key question: Why should we sequence ideas in a story?
